title: The ledger, answered
summary: Your round-1 FAQ kept as you picked it (the hero's head, a hairline ledger of six questions, one answer open, both doors beside it). The logo-symbol toggles are replaced by a drawn + that turns to −, a thin line that draws across the open question, and answers that lead with a one-line straight verdict.

reference.site: Round 1 · A ('The core, answered'), harmonised with the A×C system; ledger grammar from B
reference.borrowed: From round-1 A, everything you picked. That is the asymmetric split on graphite (after Giga), with the hero's head at left and a hairline ledger at right, the mono 01–06 index, exactly one answer open, and both doors in the left column: the red REQUEST A SYSTEM AUDIT ↗, then 'Something we didn't cover? ASK THE FOUNDING TEAM →'. The source copy stays: 'Straight answers, / before the call.', the lede, and the six questions and answers, lightly trimmed.
reference.kelwin: The section is now built on the shared A×C kit. The statement is two lines (88px, one light line) and runs wide above the split, like every round-2 head. The red rule shares one line with the ledger's top hairline, and the lede and doors sit under it as the hero's lede-and-doors block. DIRECTION-AC makes this one of two deliberately drawing-free sections, so the lead device is type: the kit's ledger that opens in place (B's grammar, as the system assigns). The three-piece mark toggles are gone, including both the ghost plates and the red core that landed in the open row. Each row now ends in the kit's drawn +, which turns to − when it opens. The open row gets a 1px --fg selection rule drawn across its top edge, the same 'active' rule the evidence cells use. Every answer opens with a wide-cut verdict ('Infrastructure you own.') above its reasoning, taking B's short answers into A's type voice. Row 01 now rests open instead of 02, so the reading path starts at the top. It also stops the FAQ from repeating, word for word, the 'ten working days · fixed scope · the readout is yours' terms that the final CTA shows directly below. The label-row meta is 'Q. 01–06', in the same grammar as every other section's 'Fig. 0n'. The only red is the primary button; the label square and the rule are family punctuation.

motion: entrance (≈2.9s, travels the reading path): the kit runs the head. The label fades in, 'Straight answers,' rises out of its mask, and 'before the call.' (light) follows 200ms behind. At 520ms the red rule and the ledger's top hairline draw left → right together (600ms / 1000ms), so the shared line is one gesture. The lede fades up 12px at 600ms. The rows then draw in order, 01 → 06: each row's hairline draws left → right (700ms, 90ms stagger from 700ms), with its index, question and + fading in behind it (500ms).

orchestrated moment (the ledger opening in place, once): at 1.6s, as the last row lands, row 01 opens. Its + turns to −, the vertical hairline rotating 90° onto the horizontal (360ms --ease-inout). A 1px --fg selection rule draws across the row's top edge (640ms), and the answer unfolds in place (360ms). The wide-cut verdict 'Infrastructure you own.' rises out of its mask (640ms --ease-out), and the reasoning fades up 8px behind it (500ms). The audit button and the contact door fade up last (2.2s / 2.3s), so the path ends on the action. The section rests at about 2.9s, with 01 open.
ambient: none. The section is the page's quiet beat before the red final call.

interaction: each row is a real button inside an h3 (aria-expanded, aria-controls), and closed answers are inert. One row is open at a time, and clicking the open row closes it. Hovering a closed question lifts it from --fg-2 to --fg and nudges it 6px right (kit). When a row closes, its − turns back to +, its rule retracts (280ms) and its answer folds (200ms) while the new row opens. The audit button deepens to --accent-hover with ↗ moving 2px up-right; the contact underline turns --fg with → moving 3px.

on the live site: the head and rows draw in once when the section is 40% visible (IntersectionObserver, no pin), and row 01 opens as the rows land. There is no automatic handover; after that the reader drives the ledger. The left column (lede and doors) can stay sticky while the ledger scrolls. With reduced motion, KM.init({reduced:true}) keeps the markup's resting state (01 open) synchronously, with no entrance and no timers.
notes: Layout: label row cols 1–12 (meta 'Q. 01–06'); statement cols 1–11 (two lines); then the left column (cols 1–5: rule, lede balanced to two lines within 24em so it stops clear of the ledger in both skins, then the doors 36px below) and the ledger (cols 6–12, 755px). Row 01 reads 'How is this different from a lead generation agency?' (the source said 'from hiring a lead generation agency'), so all six questions sit on one 24px line in both skins and the rows keep one 75px pitch. The ledger's hairlines are 1px pseudo-lines in the kit's --line / --line-2, visually identical to the kit borders, so they can draw in. The head is held at a whole 234px (it measures 233.3), so the rule and every hairline land on whole pixels. Row 01 rests open, not 02: 02's answer (ten working days, fixed scope, the readout is yours) is exactly what the final CTA's terms column shows next, and opening the top row makes the reading path start at 01. C quotas: no drawing, no callouts, no dimension lines and no registration marks (the system leaves the FAQ drawing-free). Mono is the one meta line plus the six indices.
addressed: Kept as you picked it: the hero's head, a hairline ledger of six questions, one answer open, and both doors beside it.
The logo symbol is gone from every row. Each toggle is now a drawn + that turns into − as its answer opens.
The open question is marked by a thin light line that draws across it instead of the red core. The audit button is the only red left.
Each answer starts with a short, straight verdict in the headline face ('Infrastructure you own.'), then the reasoning.

One clear reading path: the first question rests open, so you read heading → lede → 01 and its answer → the rest → the buttons. The motion runs the same way, with one answer opening once and the buttons arriving last.
No echo of the next section. The audit's 'ten working days, fixed scope' terms now appear once, in the final call, instead of twice in a row.
The heading is two lines, like the hero ('Straight answers, / before the call.'), and the red rule lines up with the ledger's top line.
No drawing here on purpose, so the page breathes between the before/after and the red final call.
